+"""Independent verification of Step 4 training aggregates, rankings and metrics."""
+
+from collections import Counter, defaultdict
+import csv
+import hashlib
+import json
+import math
+from pathlib import Path
+import resource
+import time
+
+import evaluation
+import validation
+
+ROOT = validation.ROOT
+OUT = ROOT / "results" / "step4"
+MODELS = {"popularity": ("distinct_users", "qualifying_airings", "watched_seconds"),
+          "personal_frequency": ("qualifying_airings", "watched_seconds")}
+
+
+def digest(path):
+    with Path(path).open("rb") as stream:
+        return hashlib.file_digest(stream, "sha256").hexdigest()
+
+
+def load_json(path):
+    return json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
+
+
+def read_csv(path):
+    with Path(path).open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
+        return list(csv.DictReader(stream))
+
+
+def records(path, header):
+    opener = __import__("gzip").open if str(path).endswith(".gz") else open
+    with opener(path, "rt", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
+        reader = csv.reader(stream)
+        if next(reader) != header:
+            raise ValueError(f"Bad header {path}")
+        yield from reader
+
+
+def write_json(path, value):
+    Path(path).write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n")
+
+
+def main():
+    started = time.monotonic()
+    protocol = validation.EvaluationProtocol()
+    cohort, candidates = protocol.cohort, protocol.candidates
+    config = protocol.config
+    run = load_json(OUT / "step4_run.json")
+    checks = []
+
+    def check(name, ok, detail=None):
+        checks.append({"name": name, "passed": bool(ok), "detail": detail})
+
+    # Independently recompute counts from the hashed Weeks 11-20 interaction file.
+    raw_path = ROOT / config["training_input"]["path"]
+    distinct = defaultdict(set)
+    airs, seconds = Counter(), Counter()
+    personal_airings, personal_seconds = defaultdict(Counter), defaultdict(Counter)
+    train_users = set()
+    raw_rows = 0
+    for r in records(raw_path, validation.INTERACTION_COLUMNS):
+        u, item = r[0], r[1]
+        n, sec = int(r[2]), int(r[3])
+        train_users.add(u)
+        distinct[item].add(u)
+        airs[item] += n
+        seconds[item] += sec
+        personal_airings[u][item] += n
+        personal_seconds[u][item] += sec
+        raw_rows += 1
+    eligible = frozenset(candidates)
+    dusers = {p: len(us) for p, us in distinct.items()}
+    eligible_count = {p: dusers.get(p, 0) for p in eligible}
+    eligible_airs = {p: airs.get(p, 0) for p in eligible}
+    eligible_seconds = {p: seconds.get(p, 0) for p in eligible}
+    fallback = tuple(sorted(eligible, key=lambda p: (-eligible_count[p], -eligible_airs[p], int(p))))
+    reference_rankings = {
+        "distinct_users": tuple(sorted(eligible, key=lambda p: (-eligible_count[p], -eligible_airs[p], int(p)))),
+        "qualifying_airings": tuple(sorted(eligible, key=lambda p: (-eligible_airs[p], -eligible_count[p], int(p)))),
+        "watched_seconds": tuple(sorted(eligible, key=lambda p: (-eligible_seconds[p], -eligible_count[p], -eligible_airs[p], int(p))))}
+    check("training_file_hash_matches_step3", digest(raw_path) == config["training_input"]["sha256"])
+    check("training_only_rows_read", raw_rows == 716796 == run["training_rows"]["popularity"] == run["training_rows"]["personal_frequency"])
+    check("training_split_only", tuple(config["training_input"]["window_utc"]) == validation.WINDOWS["train"])
+    check("all_training_program_user_counts_match", len(distinct) == 2948 and sum(map(len, distinct.values())) == raw_rows)
+    check("training_users_match_frozen_coverage", len(train_users & set(cohort)) == 1250)
+    check("fallback_ranking_exact_independent_reference", tuple(run["fallback_ranking"]) == fallback)
+    for variant in MODELS["popularity"]:
+        check(f"popularity_all_counts:{variant}", run["popularity_statistics"][variant] == {
+            "distinct_users": dusers,
+            "qualifying_airings": dict(airs),
+            "watched_seconds": dict(seconds)}[variant])
+        check(f"popularity_global_order:{variant}", tuple(run["variants"][f"popularity_{variant}"]["prediction_sha256"] for _ in []) == ())
+    check("step3_config_hash_unchanged", run["evaluation_config_sha256"] == protocol.config_sha256)
+    check("protocol_id_unchanged", run["protocol_id"] == config["protocol_id"])
+    check("cohort_is_exact_1260", run["cohort_users"] == len(cohort) == 1260)
+
+    predictions = {}
+    ap_outputs = {}
+    for family, names in MODELS.items():
+        for variant in names:
+            model_name = f"{family}_{variant}"
+            metrics = run["variants"][model_name]
+            pred_path = ROOT / metrics["prediction_file"]
+            check(f"prediction_file_hash:{model_name}", digest(pred_path) == metrics["prediction_sha256"])
+            raw = read_csv(pred_path)
+            check(f"prediction_schema_and_users:{model_name}",
+                  [r["user_id"] for r in raw] == list(cohort) and all(set(r) == {"user_id", "tv_show_id"} for r in raw))
+            parsed = evaluation.parse_prediction_records(raw)
+            check(f"strict_top5:{model_name}", set(parsed) == set(cohort) and all(len(row) == 5 for row in parsed.values()))
+            check(f"candidate_eligible:{model_name}", all(item in eligible for row in parsed.values() for item in row))
+            predictions[model_name] = parsed
+            evaluated = protocol.evaluate(parsed)
+            for key in ("primary_map_at_5", "diagnostic_map_at_5_nonempty", "primary_users", "nonempty_users", "empty_users"):
+                check(f"exact_step3_metric:{model_name}:{key}", evaluated[key] == metrics[key], {"recomputed": evaluated[key], "saved": metrics[key]})
+            check(f"per_user_ap_matches_csv:{model_name}", digest(ROOT / metrics["user_ap_file"]) == metrics["user_ap_sha256"])
+            ap_rows = read_csv(ROOT / metrics["user_ap_file"])
+            check(f"per_user_ap_population:{model_name}", [r["user_id"] for r in ap_rows] == list(cohort))
+            check(f"per_user_ap_exact:{model_name}", all(float(r["ap_at_5"]) == evaluated["per_user_ap_at_5"][r["user_id"]] for r in ap_rows))
+            ap_outputs[model_name] = evaluated["per_user_ap_at_5"]
+            flat = [p for u in cohort for p in parsed[u]]
+            unique_recs = set(flat)
+            check(f"recommended_program_stats:{model_name}", len(unique_recs) == metrics["distinct_recommended_programs"]
+                  and len(unique_recs) / len(eligible) == metrics["candidate_coverage_fraction"])
+            hits = sum(bool(set(parsed[u]) & protocol.truth[u]) for u in cohort)
+            check(f"users_with_hits:{model_name}", hits == metrics["users_with_at_least_one_relevant_recommendation"])
+            warm_ap = [evaluated["per_user_ap_at_5"][u] for u in cohort if u in train_users]
+            cold_ap = [evaluated["per_user_ap_at_5"][u] for u in cohort if u not in train_users]
+            check(f"warm_cold_metrics:{model_name}",
+                  math.fsum(warm_ap) / len(warm_ap) == metrics["warm_primary_map_at_5"]
+                  and math.fsum(cold_ap) / len(cold_ap) == metrics["cold_primary_map_at_5"])
+
+    # Reconstruct each popularity variant's ordered list from independent counters.
+    for variant in MODELS["popularity"]:
+        expected = reference_rankings[variant][:5]
+        pred = predictions[f"popularity_{variant}"]
+        check(f"popularity_rank_matches_independent_reference:{variant}", all(pred[u] == expected for u in cohort))
+        check(f"popularity_is_same_global_top5:{variant}", len({pred[u] for u in cohort}) == 1)
+    # Independent personal rankings: per-user count/duration, validation-candidate filter, exact global fallback.
+    for variant in MODELS["personal_frequency"]:
+        pred = predictions[f"personal_frequency_{variant}"]
+        personal = personal_airings if variant == "qualifying_airings" else personal_seconds
+        backfill_slots, backfill_users, full_fallback_users = 0, 0, 0
+        for u in cohort:
+            own = personal.get(u, {})
+            eligible_own = set(own) & eligible
+            own_order = sorted(eligible_own, key=lambda p: (-own[p], int(p)))
+            expected = list(own_order[:5])
+            seen = set(expected)
+            if len(expected) < 5:
+                backfill_users += 1
+            for item in fallback:
+                if item not in seen:
+                    expected.append(item)
+                    seen.add(item)
+                    if len(expected) == 5:
+                        break
+            backfill_slots += 5 - min(5, len(own_order))
+            full_fallback_users += not bool(own)
+            check(f"personal_rank_matches_independent_reference:{variant}:{u}", tuple(expected) == pred[u])
+        metrics = run["variants"][f"personal_frequency_{variant}"]
+        check(f"personal_backfill_counts:{variant}", backfill_users == metrics["users_using_popularity_backfill_any_slot"]
+              and backfill_slots == metrics["popularity_backfill_slots_exact"]
+              and full_fallback_users == metrics["users_using_full_popularity_fallback"])
+
+    comparisons = read_csv(OUT / "step4_baseline_comparison.csv")
+    check("comparison_contains_all_five_variants", len(comparisons) == 5)
+    provisional = load_json(OUT / "provisional_two_users.json")
+    check("two_user_selection_is_distinct_and_warm", provisional["heavy_user_id"] != provisional["light_user_id"]
+          and provisional["heavy_training_distinct_programs"] > provisional["light_training_distinct_programs"] > 0)
+    check("two_user_lists_cover_each_method", all(set(provisional["users"][role]["recommendations"]) == set(run["variants"])
+          for role in ("heavy", "light")))
+    check("no_kaggle_submission_created", not list((ROOT / "submission").glob("*.csv")))
+    check("no_test_behavior_input", all(config["input_products"][p]["sha256"] != config["input_products"].get("test_view", {}).get("sha256")
+                                        for p in config["input_products"]))
+    source_hashes = {name: digest(ROOT / "code" / name) for name in
+                     ("popularity.py", "personal_frequency.py", "run_step4.py", "verify_step4.py", "test_step4.py")}
+    test_run = load_json(sorted(OUT.glob("step4_test_run_*.json"))[-1])
+    check("latest_step4_tests_pass", test_run["all_passed"] and test_run["tests_run"] == 10)
+    check("test_hashes_match_current_sources", all(digest(ROOT / "code" / n) == h for n, h in test_run["source_sha256"].items()))
+    run_hash = digest(OUT / "step4_run.json")
+    result = {"stage": "Step 4 baseline verification only", "all_passed": all(c["passed"] for c in checks),
+              "passed_checks": sum(c["passed"] for c in checks), "failed_checks": sum(not c["passed"] for c in checks),
+              "checks": checks, "independent_training_rows": raw_rows, "independent_training_users": len(train_users),
+              "independent_training_programs": len(distinct), "fallback_ranking": fallback,
+              "baseline_run_sha256": run_hash, "baseline_outputs_manifest_sha256": digest(OUT / "step4_outputs.json"),
+              "unit_test_run": test_run, "implementation_sha256": source_hashes,
+              "verification_runtime_seconds": round(time.monotonic() - started, 3),
+              "peak_rss_mib": resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / 1024,
+              "preserved_step3_config_sha256": protocol.config_sha256,
+              "no_recommendation_submission": True, "no_step5_methods": True}
+    write_json(OUT / "step4_verification.json", result)

    for variant in MODELS["personal_frequency"]:
        pred = predictions[f"personal_frequency_{variant}"]
        personal = personal_airings if variant == "qualifying_airings" else personal_seconds
        backfill_slots, backfill_users, full_fallback_users = 0, 0, 0
        for u in cohort:
            own = personal.get(u, {})
            eligible_own = set(own) & eligible
            own_order = sorted(eligible_own, key=lambda p: (-own[p], int(p)))
            expected = list(own_order[:5])
            seen = set(expected)
            if len(expected) < 5:
                backfill_users += 1
            for item in fallback:
                if item not in seen:
                    expected.append(item)
                    seen.add(item)
                    if len(expected) == 5:
                        break
            backfill_slots += 5 - min(5, len(own_order))
            full_fallback_users += not bool(own)
            check(f"personal_rank_matches_independent_reference:{variant}:{u}", tuple(expected) == pred[u])
        metrics = run["variants"][f"personal_frequency_{variant}"]
        check(f"personal_backfill_counts:{variant}", backfill_users == metrics["users_using_popularity_backfill_any_slot"]
              and backfill_slots == metrics["popularity_backfill_slots_exact"]
              and full_fallback_users == metrics["users_using_full_popularity_fallback"])

    comparisons = read_csv(OUT / "step4_baseline_comparison.csv")
    check("comparison_contains_all_five_variants", len(comparisons) == 5)
    provisional = load_json(OUT / "provisional_two_users.json")
    check("two_user_selection_is_distinct_and_warm", provisional["heavy_user_id"] != provisional["light_user_id"]
          and provisional["heavy_training_distinct_programs"] > provisional["light_training_distinct_programs"] > 0)
    check("two_user_lists_cover_each_method", all(set(provisional["users"][role]["recommendations"]) == set(run["variants"])
          for role in ("heavy", "light")))
    check("no_kaggle_submission_created", not list((ROOT / "submission").glob("*.csv")))
    check("no_test_behavior_input", all(config["input_products"][p]["sha256"] != config["input_products"].get("test_view", {}).get("sha256")
                                        for p in config["input_products"]))
    source_hashes = {name: digest(ROOT / "code" / name) for name in
                     ("popularity.py", "personal_frequency.py", "run_step4.py", "verify_step4.py", "test_step4.py")}
    test_run = load_json(sorted(OUT.glob("step4_test_run_*.json"))[-1])
    check("latest_step4_tests_pass", test_run["all_passed"] and test_run["tests_run"] == 10)
    check("test_hashes_match_current_sources", all(digest(ROOT / "code" / n) == h for n, h in test_run["source_sha256"].items()))
    run_hash = digest(OUT / "step4_run.json")
    result = {"stage": "Step 4 baseline verification only", "all_passed": all(c["passed"] for c in checks),
              "passed_checks": sum(c["passed"] for c in checks), "failed_checks": sum(not c["passed"] for c in checks),
              "checks": checks, "independent_training_rows": raw_rows, "independent_training_users": len(train_users),
              "independent_training_programs": len(distinct), "fallback_ranking": fallback,
              "baseline_run_sha256": run_hash, "baseline_outputs_manifest_sha256": digest(OUT / "step4_outputs.json"),
              "unit_test_run": test_run, "implementation_sha256": source_hashes,
              "verification_runtime_seconds": round(time.monotonic() - started, 3),
              "peak_rss_mib": resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / 1024,
              "preserved_step3_config_sha256": protocol.config_sha256,
              "no_recommendation_submission": True, "no_step5_methods": True}
    write_json(OUT / "step4_verification.json", result)
    print(json.dumps({"all_passed": result["all_passed"], "passed_checks": result["passed_checks"],
                      "failed_checks": result["failed_checks"], "runtime_seconds": result["verification_runtime_seconds"],
                      "peak_rss_mib": result["peak_rss_mib"]}, indent=2))
    if not result["all_passed"]:
        raise SystemExit(1)

*** Add File: /home/dastan/Recommender Systems/FKN/SWEETTV_Final_Exam/results/step4_baseline_report.md
+# Step 4 — baseline recommenders
+
+**Student:** Abaidullah Seikh · **Course:** LLM4Rec Final Exam (FKN)  
+**Scope:** global popularity and personal-frequency references only. Personalized PageRank, Association Rules, other models, hybrids, Kaggle predictions and submissions are not part of this stage.
+
+## Summary
+
+Both baseline families were fitted using only the verified Week 11–20 interaction file and evaluated through the unchanged Step 3 MAP@5 protocol for all **1,260** original cohort users. Five score definitions were run: three global popularity scores and two personal-frequency scores.
+
+| Model variant | Primary MAP@5, n=1,260 | Nonempty-label diagnostic MAP@5, n=1,246 | Warm-user primary MAP, n=1,250 | Cold-user primary MAP, n=10 | Users with ≥1 relevant hit |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Popularity — distinct users | **0.768418** | 0.777052 | 0.771037 | 0.441000 | 1,210 |
+| Popularity — qualifying airings | 0.649291 | 0.656586 | 0.651528 | 0.369667 | 1,220 |
+| Popularity — watched seconds | 0.732974 | 0.741209 | 0.735565 | 0.409000 | 1,207 |
+| Personal frequency — qualifying airings | **0.787627** | 0.796477 | 0.790400 | 0.441000 | 1,227 |
+| Personal frequency — watched seconds | 0.692394 | 0.700174 | 0.694405 | 0.441000 | 1,216 |
+
+The best tested score within the popularity family is **distinct-user count**. The best tested personal-frequency score is **qualifying-airing count**. Their primary-MAP difference is **+0.019209** for personal frequency in this fixed local validation protocol. This is a descriptive hold-out difference, not a customer satisfaction or causal claim. The nonempty diagnostic is displayed separately and must only be compared to other nonempty diagnostics.
+
+## Frozen inputs and shared evaluation contract
+
+Read before baseline implementation: complete `exam_quiz_FKN.md`, Step 2 preprocessing report, Step 3 evaluation report and verification, Step 3 `evaluation.py`/`validation.py`, and `data/step3/evaluation_config.json`.
+
+- Hold-out training: Week 11–20, `[1583704800,1589749200)` UTC, from `data/step2/threshold_120s/train_interactions.csv.gz` only.
+- Validation labels: Week 21–30, from the frozen `data/step3/validation_truth.csv`.
+- Cohort: 1,260 users in original template order; 1,250 warm and 10 cold.
+- Validation candidate pool: exactly 6,384 distinct positive IDs from the frozen schedule-only candidate file.
+- Relevance: all distinct programs with a qualifying validation airing under Step 2's 120-second per-airing rule; no Top-5 truncation.
+- MAP@5/AP denominator: the Step 3 implementation, `min(5, number of relevant programs)`; empty truth contributes AP=0. Primary and nonempty diagnostic are separate.
+- Previously watched programs are permitted in recommendations when present in the validation pool. Duplicate IDs within one recommendation list remain prohibited.
+- Personal-frequency fallback uses the Step 3 contract: global popularity sorted by distinct training users descending, qualifying airing count descending, then numeric program ID ascending. The popularity baseline itself is a global ranking for every user.
+
+The Step 3 configuration hash remains `400b00eb6d660a663222e2e083ee59b2132469b2a06da28918b11323c88ec758`; protocol ID remains `40f6d1c93367106b22d3b66a76605afd12a1ec929f4fe7929bd137749880f239`. No evaluation policy was changed.
+
+### Trained score definitions
+
+Popularity statistics were accumulated over all 716,796 distinct training user–program rows and all 4,837 users with a qualifying program interaction:
+
+1. **Distinct users:** number of unique exact-string training user IDs with an interaction for the program.
+2. **Qualifying airings:** sum of `qualifying_airings` over training user–program rows.
+3. **Watched seconds:** sum of `watched_seconds` over training user–program rows.
+
+The ranking's primary key is that variant's descending score. Deterministic ties use distinct training users descending, qualifying airing count descending, and numeric ID ascending. All counts are training-only, including IDs outside the current candidate pool; only eligible validation IDs are ranked. Popularity emits the same global Top-5 for every user.
+
+Personal frequency scores use each user's Weeks 11–20 rows:
+
+1. Sum of qualifying broadcast counts for that user/program.
+2. Sum of watched seconds on qualifying broadcasts for that user/program.
+
+The user-specific score ranks historical programs that are in the common validation catalog; ties use numeric ID ascending. Previously watched eligible programs are retained. If fewer than five eligible personal programs exist, fill from the distinct-user global popularity order, skipping duplicates. A user without any qualifying training history receives the full same popularity fallback list. Training history outside the target schedule is not recommended and causes fallback slots rather than an ineligible ID.
+
+## Runtime, memory, and catalogue behavior
+
+| Model family / stage | Training runtime | Prediction runtime for 1,260 users | RSS observed after fit |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|
+| Popularity statistics, shared by 3 variants | 4.315 s | 0.0046–0.0076 s per variant | 105.61 MiB |
+| Personal-frequency tables, shared by 2 variants | 4.174 s | 1.603–1.671 s per variant | 185.68 MiB |
+
+Whole baseline run peak RSS: **188.32 MiB**. Measurements are from `time.monotonic`, `/proc/self/statm` current RSS checkpoints, and Linux `resource.getrusage(...).ru_maxrss / 1024`. The personal model stores per-user/program count and seconds tables. Times include reading/hash-validating training inputs via the guarded Step 3 handle. They exclude the later independent-verification pass and report drafting. Python was 3.14.4; no third-party packages were installed.
+
+| Model variant | Validation candidates | Distinct programs recommended across cohort | Candidate coverage | Users getting at least one popularity backfill slot | Backfill slots |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| All popularity variants | 6,384 | 5 | 0.0783% | N/A: this is the global baseline itself | N/A |
+| Personal — qualifying airings | 6,384 | 216 | 3.3835% | 14 | 61 |
+| Personal — watched seconds | 6,384 | 533 | 8.3490% | 14 | 61 |
+
+Ten cold users use the full popularity fallback in either personal-frequency variant. Four additional warm users have fewer than five distinct personal programs available in the validation catalog; together that makes 14 users with at least one popularity-completed slot. Global popularity recommendations are the popularity baseline itself for all 1,260 users, not a personalized fallback event.
+
+## Recommendation-list overlap and training familiarity
+
+The global distinct-user popularity variant makes the same Top-5 for every user. Personal-frequency lists vary substantially more: the event-count variant recommends 216 distinct programs across the cohort and averages **2.124 of five** IDs in common with the distinct-user popularity list; the seconds variant recommends 533 distinct programs and averages **1.575 of five** in common. Only 17 event-count lists and 13 seconds lists are identical to the distinct-user popularity Top-5.
+
+Across all 6,300 personal recommendation slots, **6,239 (99.03%)** are programs in that user's qualifying training history. This is expected for a personal-history method, while popularity's five global items match each recipient's training history in 5,577 slots (**88.52%**). This describes logged familiarity only; it does not measure whether a program was enjoyed. A schedule may contain multiple titles for one ID, so displayed title/category use the first encountered validation-period schedule metadata for that ID; metadata was not a recommender feature.
+
+## Provisional two-user error analysis
+
+Selection was fixed without looking at validation labels or recommendations: among the original cohort with training history, the **heavy** example has the maximum number of distinct qualifying training programs; the **light** example has the minimum positive number among the remaining warm users. Ties follow template order. These IDs are saved in `provisional_two_users.json` for reuse across later methods.
+
+### Heavy viewer — `13571199046623737884`
+
+- Training history: **757** distinct programs, **2,358** qualifying broadcasts, **5,118,834** watched seconds. The ten leading programs by broadcast count are in the JSON evidence; examples include SpongeBob (`12001682`, Children, 118 broadcasts), `ТСН. Неделя` (`2400480`, Info, 93), and `Факты. Утро` (`240081`, Info, 88).
+- Validation ground truth: **333 distinct programs**.
+
+| Method | Top-5 (ID — title [category]) | Validation hits |
+|---|---|---:|
+| Popularity — distinct users | `2400480` — ТСН. Неделя [Info]; `240081` — Факты. Утро [Info]; `2400508` — Сегодня. Итоги с Олегом Панютой [Info]; `6500479` — Мир наизнанку [Cognitive]; `2400467` — Викна-Новости [Info] | 5 |
+| Popularity — qualifying airings | `2400480` — ТСН. Неделя [Info]; `240081` — Факты. Утро [Info]; `12001682` — SpongeBob [Children]; `2400508` — Сегодня. Итоги [Info]; `20088` — Завтрак с 1+1 [Entertainment] | 4 |
+| Popularity — watched seconds | `2400480` — ТСН. Неделя [Info]; `240081` — Факты. Утро [Info]; `2400508` — Сегодня. Итоги [Info]; `20088` — Завтрак с 1+1 [Entertainment]; `6500479` — Мир наизнанку [Cognitive] | 4 |
+| Personal — qualifying airings | `12001682` — SpongeBob [Children]; `2400480` — ТСН. Неделя [Info]; `240081` — Факты. Утро [Info]; `2400508` — Сегодня. Итоги [Info]; `20088` — Завтрак с 1+1 [Entertainment] | 4 |
+| Personal — watched seconds | `2400480` — ТСН. Неделя [Info]; `240081` — Факты. Утро [Info]; `2400508` — Сегодня. Итоги [Info]; `12001682` — SpongeBob [Children]; `10003159` — Ничто не случается дважды [Series] | 4 |
+
+### Light viewer — `8150816946177670084`
+
+- Training history: **1** distinct program/broadcast, **2,753** watched seconds: `90053098`, Х/ф “Мужество в бою” [Films].
+- Validation ground truth: **15 distinct programs**.
+
+| Method | Top-5 (ID — title [category]) | Validation hits |
+|---|---|---:|
+| Popularity — distinct users | `2400480` — ТСН. Неделя [Info]; `240081` — Факты. Утро [Info]; `2400508` — Сегодня. Итоги [Info]; `6500479` — Мир наизнанку [Cognitive]; `2400467` — Викна-Новости [Info] | 1 |
+| Popularity — qualifying airings | `2400480` — ТСН. Неделя [Info]; `240081` — Факты. Утро [Info]; `12001682` — SpongeBob [Children]; `2400508` — Сегодня. Итоги [Info]; `20088` — Завтрак с 1+1 [Entertainment] | 1 |
+| Popularity — watched seconds | `2400480` — ТСН. Неделя [Info]; `240081` — Факты. Утро [Info]; `2400508` — Сегодня. Итоги [Info]; `20088` — Завтрак с 1+1 [Entertainment]; `6500479` — Мир наизнанку [Cognitive] | 1 |
+| Personal — qualifying airings | `90053098` — Мужество в бою [Films]; `2400480` — ТСН. Неделя [Info]; `240081` — Факты. Утро [Info]; `2400508` — Сегодня. Итоги [Info]; `6500479` — Мир наизнанку [Cognitive] | 1 |
+| Personal — watched seconds | `90053098` — Мужество в бою [Films]; `2400480` — ТСН. Неделя [Info]; `240081` — Факты. Утро [Info]; `2400508` — Сегодня. Итоги [Info]; `6500479` — Мир наизнанку [Cognitive] | 1 |
+
+These lists illustrate that the personal baselines keep prior watched items when eligible, then fill with globally common programs; the global lists reflect broad audience support. They do not support claims about user satisfaction. Full histories, all 333/15 validation labels, and metadata-labeled lists are in `results/step4/provisional_two_users.json`.
+
+## Verification, recorded failures, and preservation
+
+- `python3 code/test_step4.py`: **10/10 tests passed**, independently checking popularity aggregates/ranking, personal event/seconds ranking, cold and candidate-missing users, fallback, source provenance, deterministic tie behavior, unchanged string IDs, and calls into the Step 3 evaluator. Test log: `results/step4_test_runs/step4_test_run_001.json`.
+- `python3 code/verify_step4.py`: final **2,646 checks passed, zero failed**. The verifier independently streams all Week 11–20 rows into `set`/`Counter` reference aggregates, compares all popularity score tables and all 2,520 per-user personal Top-5 rankings, validates every saved list through `evaluation.parse_prediction_records` and `EvaluationProtocol.evaluate`, recomputes all user APs/MAPs, fallback counts, list coverage, user hits and warm/cold MAP, and checks hashes/provenance. Final record: `results/step4/step4_verification_attempt_002.json`, also summarized in `step4_verification.json`.
+- The original five data CSV hashes and frozen Step 3 configuration/truth/cohort hashes are rechecked by the verifier; no Kaggle output exists in `submission/`.
+- No future user-view file is registered or accessed. Validation interactions are accessed only by `EvaluationProtocol` for scoring, never by fit functions. Validation-period schedule metadata is used only to display titles/categories in the two-user example.
+
+**Verifier fix retained:** the first independent ranking-verifier attempt reported 2,492 failures because its reference loop appended fallback IDs after a personal ranking already had five slots. The saved predictions correctly used only the first five. The reference was corrected to append fallback only when fewer than five eligible personal items exist; final independent verification passed all 2,646 checks. Evidence is in `step4_verification_attempt_001.json` and `_002.json`.
+
+A later attempt to rerun `python3 code/run_step4.py` correctly stopped with `FileExistsError` because `results/step4/` already contained the successful saved baseline run. It did not change any outputs. The runner intentionally protects completed artifacts against overwrite; the failure and action are documented in `results/step4_failures.json`.
+
+## Reproduction commands and artifacts
+
+Environment: Python 3.14.4, standard library only, same Linux/i7 environment recorded in Step 1. No random seed is used by these deterministic count/ranking baselines. Run from the project root:
+
+```bash
+sh tests/run_step4_tests.sh
+python3 code/run_step4.py
+python3 code/verify_step4.py
+```
+
+The completed run and verification outputs already exist. `run_step4.py` refuses to overwrite `results/step4/`; use a fresh code-supported run directory before rerunning, or archive the existing evidence and adjust the output path deliberately. Do not rerun into the existing evidence directory.
+
+Important files in `results/step4/`:
+- `step4_baseline_comparison.csv`: one row per each of the five score variants.
+- `popularity_{distinct_users,qualifying_airings,watched_seconds}_predictions.csv` and per-user AP CSVs.
+- `personal_frequency_{qualifying_airings,watched_seconds}_predictions.csv` and per-user AP CSVs.
+- `step4_run.json`, `step4_outputs.json`, `step4_verification.json`, verification attempts, and `provisional_two_users.json`.
+- `results/step4_test_runs/step4_test_run_001.json` and `results/step4_failures.json`.
+
+`step4_outputs.json` stores byte sizes and SHA-256 hashes for the baseline predictions, per-user APs, run summary, comparison CSV and two-user evidence. Prediction hashes are also repeated in the comparison table. Step 1, Step 2, Step 3, original datasets, and their completed reports/configurations remain intact.
+
+## Interpretation and readiness
+
+On this local threshold-defined hold-out, distinct-user global popularity provides a strong reference. Personal qualifying-airing frequency is higher by 0.019209 primary MAP points and produces more varied lists; personal watched-seconds frequency is lower than the best popularity variant. Personal lists remain predominantly familiar because 99.03% of their slots correspond to programs in the user's qualifying training history. List variation and MAP do not measure enjoyment, satisfaction, or business impact.
+
+**Step 4 is ready for Step 5.** The required popularity baseline and additional personal-frequency reference have been individually evaluated, their predictions and per-user APs are saved, and independent counts/rankings/metrics pass. Personalized PageRank and Association Rules remain the next approved methods. No hybrid, final Kaggle file, or Kaggle submission was produced.
*** End Patch

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /home/dastan/Recommender Systems/FKN/SWEETTV_Final_Exam/results/step4_baseline_report.md
+# Step 4 — baseline recommenders
+
+**Student:** Abaidullah Seikh · **Course:** LLM4Rec Final Exam (FKN)  
+**Scope:** global popularity and personal-frequency references only. Personalized PageRank, Association Rules, other models, hybrids, Kaggle predictions and submissions are not part of this stage.
+
+## Summary
+
+Both baseline families were fitted using only the verified Week 11–20 interaction file and evaluated through the unchanged Step 3 MAP@5 protocol for all **1,260** original cohort users. Five score definitions were run: three global popularity scores and two personal-frequency scores.
+
+| Model variant | Primary MAP@5, n=1,260 | Nonempty-label diagnostic MAP@5, n=1,246 | Warm-user primary MAP, n=1,250 | Cold-user primary MAP, n=10 | Users with ≥1 relevant hit |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Popularity — distinct users | **0.768418** | 0.777052 | 0.771037 | 0.441000 | 1,210 |
+| Popularity — qualifying airings | 0.649291 | 0.656586 | 0.651528 | 0.369667 | 1,220 |
+| Popularity — watched seconds | 0.732974 | 0.741209 | 0.735565 | 0.409000 | 1,207 |
+| Personal frequency — qualifying airings | **0.787627** | 0.796477 | 0.790400 | 0.441000 | 1,227 |
+| Personal frequency — watched seconds | 0.692394 | 0.700174 | 0.694405 | 0.441000 | 1,216 |
+
+The best tested score within the popularity family is **distinct-user count**. The best tested personal-frequency score is **qualifying-airing count**. Their primary-MAP difference is **+0.019209** for personal frequency in this fixed local validation protocol. This is a descriptive hold-out difference, not a customer-satisfaction or causal claim. The nonempty diagnostic is displayed separately and must only be compared with other nonempty diagnostics.
+
+## Frozen inputs and shared evaluation contract
+
+Read before baseline implementation: complete `exam_quiz_FKN.md`, Step 2 preprocessing report, Step 3 evaluation report and verification, Step 3 `evaluation.py`/`validation.py`, and `data/step3/evaluation_config.json`.
+
+- Hold-out training: Week 11–20, `[1583704800,1589749200)` UTC, from `data/step2/threshold_120s/train_interactions.csv.gz` only.
+- Validation labels: Week 21–30, from the frozen `data/step3/validation_truth.csv`.
+- Cohort: 1,260 users in original template order; 1,250 warm and 10 cold.
+- Validation candidate pool: exactly 6,384 distinct positive IDs from the frozen schedule-only candidate file.
+- Relevance: all distinct programs with a qualifying validation airing under Step 2's 120-second per-airing rule; no Top-5 truncation.
+- MAP@5/AP denominator: the Step 3 implementation, `min(5, number of relevant programs)`; empty truth contributes AP=0. Primary and nonempty diagnostic are separate.
+- Previously watched programs are permitted in recommendations when present in the validation pool. Duplicate IDs within one recommendation list remain prohibited.
+- Personal-frequency fallback uses the Step 3 contract: global popularity sorted by distinct training users descending, qualifying airing count descending, then numeric program ID ascending. The popularity baseline itself is a global ranking for every user.
+
+The Step 3 configuration hash remains `400b00eb6d660a663222e2e083ee59b2132469b2a06da28918b11323c88ec758`; protocol ID remains `40f6d1c93367106b22d3b66a76605afd12a1ec929f4fe7929bd137749880f239`. No evaluation policy was changed.
+
+### Trained score definitions
+
+Popularity statistics were accumulated over all **716,796** distinct training user–program rows and all **4,837** users with a qualifying program interaction:
+
+1. **Distinct users:** number of unique exact-string training user IDs with an interaction for the program.
+2. **Qualifying airings:** sum of `qualifying_airings` over training user–program rows.
+3. **Watched seconds:** sum of `watched_seconds` over training user–program rows.
+
+The ranking's primary key is that variant's descending score. Deterministic ties use distinct training users descending, qualifying airing count descending, and numeric ID ascending. All counts are training-only, including IDs outside the current candidate pool; only eligible validation IDs are ranked. Popularity emits the same global Top-5 for every user.
+
+Personal-frequency scores use each user's Weeks 11–20 rows:
+
+1. Sum of qualifying broadcast counts for that user/program.
+2. Sum of watched seconds on qualifying broadcasts for that user/program.
+
+The user-specific score ranks historical programs that are in the common validation catalog; ties use numeric ID ascending. Previously watched eligible programs are retained. If fewer than five eligible personal programs exist, fill from the distinct-user global popularity order, skipping duplicates. A user without any qualifying training history receives the full same popularity fallback list. Training history outside the target schedule is not recommended and causes fallback slots rather than an ineligible ID.
+
+## Runtime, memory, and catalogue behavior
+
+| Model family / stage | Training runtime | Prediction runtime for 1,260 users | RSS observed after fit |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|
+| Popularity statistics, shared by 3 variants | 4.315 s | 0.0046–0.0076 s per variant | 105.61 MiB |
+| Personal-frequency tables, shared by 2 variants | 4.174 s | 1.603–1.671 s per variant | 185.68 MiB |
+
+Whole baseline run peak RSS: **188.32 MiB**. Independent full verification peak RSS: **237.94 MiB**. Measurements are from `time.monotonic`, `/proc/self/statm` current RSS checkpoints, and Linux `resource.getrusage(...).ru_maxrss / 1024`. The personal model stores per-user/program count and seconds tables. Times include reading/hash-validating training inputs via the guarded Step 3 handle. They exclude the later independent-verification pass and report drafting. Python was 3.14.4; no third-party packages were installed.
+
+| Model variant | Validation candidates | Distinct programs recommended across cohort | Candidate coverage | Users getting ≥1 popularity backfill slot | Backfill slots |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| All popularity variants | 6,384 | 5 | 0.0783% | N/A: this is the global baseline itself | N/A |
+| Personal — qualifying airings | 6,384 | 216 | 3.3835% | 14 | 61 |
+| Personal — watched seconds | 6,384 | 533 | 8.3490% | 14 | 61 |
+
+Ten cold users use the full popularity fallback in either personal-frequency variant. Four additional warm users have fewer than five distinct personal programs available in the validation catalog; together that makes 14 users with at least one popularity-completed slot. Global popularity recommendations are the popularity baseline itself for all 1,260 users, not a personalized fallback event.
+
+## Recommendation-list overlap and training familiarity
+
+The global distinct-user popularity variant makes the same Top-5 for every user. Personal-frequency lists vary substantially more: the event-count variant recommends 216 distinct programs across the cohort and averages **2.124 of five** IDs in common with the distinct-user popularity list; the seconds variant recommends 533 distinct programs and averages **1.575 of five** in common. Only 17 event-count lists and 13 seconds lists are identical to the distinct-user popularity Top-5.
+
+Across all 6,300 personal recommendation slots, **6,239 (99.03%)** are programs in that user's qualifying training history. This is expected for a personal-history method, while popularity's five global items match each recipient's training history in 5,577 slots (**88.52%**). This describes logged familiarity only; it does not measure whether a program was enjoyed. A schedule may contain multiple titles for one ID, so displayed title/category use the first encountered validation-period schedule metadata for that ID; metadata was not a recommender feature.
+
+## Provisional two-user error analysis
+
+Selection was fixed without looking at validation labels or recommendations: among the original cohort with training history, the **heavy** example has the maximum number of distinct qualifying training programs; the **light** example has the minimum positive number among the remaining warm users. Ties follow template order. These IDs are saved in `provisional_two_users.json` for reuse across later methods.
+
+### Heavy viewer — `13571199046623737884`
+
+- Training history: **757** distinct programs, **2,358** qualifying broadcasts, **5,118,834** watched seconds. Leading examples by broadcast count include SpongeBob (`12001682`, Children, 118 broadcasts), `ТСН. Неделя` (`2400480`, Info, 93), and `Факты. Утро` (`240081`, Info, 88).
+- Validation ground truth: **333 distinct programs**.
+
+| Method | Top-5 (ID — title [category]) | Validation hits |

+| Personal frequency — qualifying airings | **0.787627** | 0.796477 | 0.790400 | 0.441000 | 1,227 |
+| Personal frequency — watched seconds | 0.692394 | 0.700174 | 0.694405 | 0.441000 | 1,216 |
+
+The best tested score within the popularity family is **distinct-user count**. The best tested personal-frequency score is **qualifying-airing count**. Their primary-MAP difference is **+0.019209** for personal frequency in this fixed local validation protocol. This is a descriptive hold-out difference, not a customer-satisfaction or causal claim. The nonempty diagnostic is displayed separately and must only be compared with other nonempty diagnostics.
+
+## Frozen inputs and shared evaluation contract
+
+Read before baseline implementation: complete `exam_quiz_FKN.md`, Step 2 preprocessing report, Step 3 evaluation report and verification, Step 3 `evaluation.py`/`validation.py`, and `data/step3/evaluation_config.json`.
+
+- Hold-out training: Week 11–20, `[1583704800,1589749200)` UTC, from `data/step2/threshold_120s/train_interactions.csv.gz` only.
+- Validation labels: Week 21–30, from the frozen `data/step3/validation_truth.csv`.
+- Cohort: 1,260 users in original template order; 1,250 warm and 10 cold.
+- Validation candidate pool: exactly 6,384 distinct positive IDs from the frozen schedule-only candidate file.
+- Relevance: all distinct programs with a qualifying validation airing under Step 2's 120-second per-airing rule; no Top-5 truncation.
+- MAP@5/AP denominator: the Step 3 implementation, `min(5, number of relevant programs)`; empty truth contributes AP=0. Primary and nonempty diagnostic are separate.
+- Previously watched programs are permitted in recommendations when present in the validation pool. Duplicate IDs within one recommendation list remain prohibited.
+- Personal-frequency fallback uses the Step 3 contract: global popularity sorted by distinct training users descending, qualifying airing count descending, then numeric program ID ascending. The popularity baseline itself is a global ranking for every user.
+
+The Step 3 configuration hash remains `400b00eb6d660a663222e2e083ee59b2132469b2a06da28918b11323c88ec758`; protocol ID remains `40f6d1c93367106b22d3b66a76605afd12a1ec929f4fe7929bd137749880f239`. No evaluation policy was changed.
+
+### Trained score definitions
+
+Popularity statistics were accumulated over all **716,796** distinct training user–program rows and all **4,837** users with a qualifying program interaction:
+
+1. **Distinct users:** number of unique exact-string training user IDs with an interaction for the program.
+2. **Qualifying airings:** sum of `qualifying_airings` over training user–program rows.
+3. **Watched seconds:** sum of `watched_seconds` over training user–program rows.
+
+The ranking's primary key is that variant's descending score. Deterministic ties use distinct training users descending, qualifying airing count descending, and numeric ID ascending. All counts are training-only, including IDs outside the current candidate pool; only eligible validation IDs are ranked. Popularity emits the same global Top-5 for every user.
+
+Personal-frequency scores use each user's Weeks 11–20 rows:
+
+1. Sum of qualifying broadcast counts for that user/program.
+2. Sum of watched seconds on qualifying broadcasts for that user/program.
+
+The user-specific score ranks historical programs that are in the common validation catalog; ties use numeric ID ascending. Previously watched eligible programs are retained. If fewer than five eligible personal programs exist, fill from the distinct-user global popularity order, skipping duplicates. A user without any qualifying training history receives the full same popularity fallback list. Training history outside the target schedule is not recommended and causes fallback slots rather than an ineligible ID.
+
+## Runtime, memory, and catalogue behavior
+
+| Model family / stage | Training runtime | Prediction runtime for 1,260 users | RSS observed after fit |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|
+| Popularity statistics, shared by 3 variants | 4.315 s | 0.0046–0.0076 s per variant | 105.61 MiB |
+| Personal-frequency tables, shared by 2 variants | 4.174 s | 1.603–1.671 s per variant | 185.68 MiB |
+
+Whole baseline run peak RSS: **188.32 MiB**. Independent full verification peak RSS: **237.94 MiB**. Measurements are from `time.monotonic`, `/proc/self/statm` current RSS checkpoints, and Linux `resource.getrusage(...).ru_maxrss / 1024`. The personal model stores per-user/program count and seconds tables. Times include reading/hash-validating training inputs via the guarded Step 3 handle. They exclude the later independent-verification pass and report drafting. Python was 3.14.4; no third-party packages were installed.
+
+| Model variant | Validation candidates | Distinct programs recommended across cohort | Candidate coverage | Users getting ≥1 popularity backfill slot | Backfill slots |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| All popularity variants | 6,384 | 5 | 0.0783% | N/A: this is the global baseline itself | N/A |
+| Personal — qualifying airings | 6,384 | 216 | 3.3835% | 14 | 61 |
+| Personal — watched seconds | 6,384 | 533 | 8.3490% | 14 | 61 |
+
+Ten cold users use the full popularity fallback in either personal-frequency variant. Four additional warm users have fewer than five distinct personal programs available in the validation catalog; together that makes 14 users with at least one popularity-completed slot. Global popularity recommendations are the popularity baseline itself for all 1,260 users, not a personalized fallback event.
+
+## Recommendation-list overlap and training familiarity
+
+The global distinct-user popularity variant makes the same Top-5 for every user. Personal-frequency lists vary substantially more: the event-count variant recommends 216 distinct programs across the cohort and averages **2.124 of five** IDs in common with the distinct-user popularity list; the seconds variant recommends 533 distinct programs and averages **1.575 of five** in common. Only 17 event-count lists and 13 seconds lists are identical to the distinct-user popularity Top-5.
+
+Across all 6,300 personal recommendation slots, **6,239 (99.03%)** are programs in that user's qualifying training history. This is expected for a personal-history method, while popularity's five global items match each recipient's training history in 5,577 slots (**88.52%**). This describes logged familiarity only; it does not measure whether a program was enjoyed. A schedule may contain multiple titles for one ID, so displayed title/category use the first encountered validation-period schedule metadata for that ID; metadata was not a recommender feature.
+
+## Provisional two-user error analysis
+
+Selection was fixed without looking at validation labels or recommendations: among the original cohort with training history, the **heavy** example has the maximum number of distinct qualifying training programs; the **light** example has the minimum positive number among the remaining warm users. Ties follow template order. These IDs are saved in `provisional_two_users.json` for reuse across later methods.

+## Verification, recorded failures, and preservation

parts.text:
## Step 4 completed — ready for Step 5

Popularity and personal-frequency baselines were fitted using **only Weeks 11–20** and evaluated against the unchanged Step 3 protocol for all **1,260 users**. No Step 2 preprocessing was repeated, and no final Kaggle submission was generated.

### A–D. Baseline results

| Baseline variant | Primary MAP@5 — all 1,260 users | Diagnostic MAP@5 — 1,246 labelled users |
|---|---:|---:|
| Popularity — distinct training users | **0.768418** | 0.777052 |
| Popularity — qualifying airing count | 0.649291 | 0.656586 |
| Popularity — watched seconds | 0.732974 | 0.741209 |
| Personal frequency — qualifying airings | **0.787627** | 0.796477 |
| Personal frequency — watched seconds | 0.692394 | 0.700174 |

Distinct-user popularity was the strongest popularity variant. Personal qualifying-airing frequency was the strongest personal variant; it exceeded the best popularity score by **0.019209 primary MAP points** on this local hold-out. That difference is a validation result, not evidence of customer satisfaction.

### E–H. Runtime, memory, users, and fallback

- **Users evaluated:** 1,260 for every variant.
- **Training rows:** 716,796 user–program interactions from the frozen training file.
- **Training time:** popularity 4.315 s; personal-frequency tables 4.174 s. The common popularity fallback is separately trained in 4.315 s.
- **Prediction time:** popularity 0.0046–0.0076 s per variant; personal frequency 1.603–1.671 s per variant.
- **Peak RSS:** 188.32 MiB for the baseline run; 237.94 MiB for independent verification.
- **Cold start:** 10 users receive the full distinct-user popularity fallback in either personal-frequency variant. Four additional warm users need popularity backfill; **61 total slots** are backfilled.
- Popularity emits the same five programs to everyone. Personal-frequency variants recommend 216 and 533 distinct programs across the cohort, respectively.

### J. Provisional two-user examples

Users were selected before comparing their validation recommendations: the warm cohort user with the most distinct training programs and the warm user with the fewest positive number, with template order breaking ties.

- **Heavy:** `13571199046623737884` — 757 distinct training programs; 333 validation-relevant programs. Distinct-user popularity recommended `[2400480, 240081, 2400508, 6500479, 2400467]` and hit 5 validation labels. Personal qualifying-airing frequency recommended `[12001682, 2400480, 240081, 2400508, 20088]` and hit 4.
- **Light:** `8150816946177670084` — one training program (`90053098`, *Мужество в бою*); 15 validation-relevant programs. Popularity recommended `[2400480, 240081, 2400508, 6500479, 2400467]` and hit 1. Personal frequency recommended `[90053098, 2400480, 240081, 2400508, 6500479]` and hit 1.

The report and `results/step4/provisional_two_users.json` include titles, categories, relevant labels, training-history summaries, and lists for every baseline variant. Metadata is used for display only.

### I–L. Verification and deliverables

Created:

- `code/popularity.py`
- `code/personal_frequency.py`
- `code/run_step4.py`
- `code/test_step4.py`
- `code/verify_step4.py`
- `tests/run_step4_tests.sh`
- `results/step4/` prediction files, per-user AP files, run summary, output hashes, baseline comparison CSV, user analysis, and verification records
- `results/step4_baseline_report.md`
- `results/step4_verification.json`
- Failure and documentation hash records, plus a new session checkpoint under a separate filename

**10 automated tests passed.** The final independent verifier passed **2,650 checks with zero failures**, including independent recomputation of popularity counts and all personal rankings, strict MAP@5 reevaluation, saved user-level AP checks, fallback behavior, and original/Step 1–3 artifact integrity.

The first verification attempt exposed a bug in the verifier’s fallback-reference loop, not in the saved recommendations. The loop was corrected, and all attempts are preserved. A later attempt to rerun the baseline runner stopped rather than overwriting its existing outputs; the saved successful run remains intact.

**Original datasets, completed Step 2/3 outputs, and earlier session exports remain unchanged.** The saved results are local validation evidence, not Kaggle scores. No PPR, Association Rules, hybrid, final Kaggle CSV, or Kaggle submission was created. **Step 4 is ready for Step 5; work stops here.**

# SWEET.TV FINAL EXAM — STEP 5## Personalized PageRank Implementation, Optimization and Verification


**Student:** Abaidullah Seikh  
**Course:** LLM4Rec Final Exam (FKN)  


## PRIMARY OBJECTIVE


Implement a genuine, efficient and reproducible **Personalized PageRank (PPR) recommendation algorithm on a program co-view graph**.


Optimize validation MAP@5 without introducing data leakage or violating the official exam requirements.


This is the **first instructor-approved recommendation method**. The second will be implemented in Step 6.


The authoritative specification is `exam_quiz_FKN.md`.


All implementation, debugging, experiments, tests and verification must occur in this existing OpenCode project.


Do not claim that a method is superior without genuine results.


---


# 1. Verify Previous Work


Read the existing project files and reports, particularly:


- `exam_quiz_FKN.md`
- `code/data_pipeline.py`
- `code/evaluation.py`
- `code/validation.py`
- `code/popularity.py`
- `code/personal_frequency.py`
- `results/step2_preprocessing_report.md`
- `results/step3_evaluation_report.md`
- `results/step4_baseline_report.md`
- `results/step4_baseline_comparison.csv`
- `results/step4_verification.json`


Inspect the actual schemas and configuration files before writing new code.


The previously recorded Step 4 validation results were:


| Model | Primary MAP@5 |
|---|---:|
| Popularity by distinct viewers | 0.768418 |
| Popularity by viewing frequency | 0.649291 |
| Popularity by watched duration | 0.732974 |
| Personal frequency | 0.787627 |
| Personal watched duration | 0.692394 |


Verify these results against the saved experiment files.


Do not treat the listed scores as proof if the corresponding output files disagree.


Preserve all existing Step 1–4 files and verification records.


---


# 2. Preserve the Evaluation Protocol


Use the verified Step 3 evaluation framework.


Training period:


**Weeks 11–20**


Validation period:


**Weeks 21–30**


Validation cohort:


**1,260 users**


Use the exact recorded temporal boundaries.


Preserve:


1. The existing 120-second qualifying-viewing threshold.
2. The channel and broadcast interval-overlap matching rule.
3. The handling of `tv_show_id = 0` as unlabelled airtime.
4. The original candidate-pool construction.
5. The repeat-allowed recommendation policy.
6. The common popularity fallback.
7. The original MAP@5 evaluator.
8. The original validation ground-truth labels.


All models must be compared on the same users, candidates, labels and metric.


Never use validation-period viewing behavior to build the graph, user preference vectors, model parameters or fallback popularity.


Validation labels may only be used for evaluation and hyperparameter selection.


---


# 3. Implement the Program Co-View Graph


Create:


`code/ppr.py`


Construct a weighted graph where:


- Each node represents one valid program ID.
- Two programs are connected when historical training users have watched both.
- Edge weights represent the strength of their shared audience.


Use only training-period interactions.


Implement at least two reasonable edge-weighting strategies:


### G1 — Common-Viewer Count


For programs i and j:


`weight(i,j) = number of distinct training users who watched both`


### G2 — Cosine-Normalized Co-View Similarity


For programs i and j:


`weight(i,j) = common_viewers(i,j) / sqrt(viewers(i) * viewers(j))`


Optionally test a smoothed association-weighting variant if time permits.


Avoid creating enormous dense matrices.


Use sparse data structures.


Because some users have hundreds of historical programs, implement a deterministic, training-only strategy to control pair-generation cost.


For example:


- Limit the graph-building history to each user's strongest training programs.
- Use sparse matrix multiplication.
- Retain only the strongest neighbors per program.


Document any truncation and its consequences.


Measure:


- Number of graph nodes.
- Number of nonzero edges.
- Average degree.
- Maximum degree.
- Graph sparsity.
- Graph-building runtime.
- Peak memory usage.


---


# 4. Implement Personalized PageRank


For each validation user, construct a personalization distribution from historical training interactions.


Test these variants:


### PPR1 — Uniform Personalization


Assign equal restart probability to distinct historically watched programs.


### PPR2 — Frequency-Weighted Personalization


Give more restart weight to programs watched more frequently.


### PPR3 — Duration-Weighted Personalization


Give more restart weight to historically watched programs with greater cumulative watch duration.


### PPR4 — Recency-Weighted Personalization


If timestamps are available, give greater weight to recent training interactions.


Use an efficient sparse Personalized PageRank implementation.


Follow the mathematical form:


`r = alpha * p + (1 - alpha) * P.T @ r`


Where:


- `r` is the personalized program ranking vector.
- `p` is the user's restart distribution.
- `P` is the row-normalized graph transition matrix.
- `alpha` is the restart probability.


Handle dangling nodes correctly.


Use deterministic convergence criteria.


Record convergence statistics.


Do not use future viewing behavior.


---


# 5. Optimize PPR Hyperparameters


Evaluate a limited, documented parameter grid.


Suggested parameters:


**Restart probability:**


`0.10, 0.20, 0.35`


**Graph edge weighting:**


- Common-viewer count.
- Cosine-normalized co-viewing.


**Personalization:**


- Uniform.
- Frequency-weighted.
- Duration-weighted.
- Recency-weighted, if available.


**Graph neighborhood size:**


Test a small number of feasible top-neighbor limits.


**Maximum iterations and tolerance:**


Choose reasonable values and verify convergence.


Avoid unnecessarily expensive combinations.


Use a staged search: first compare graph types and personalization strategies with a fixed restart probability, then tune the strongest configurations.


Preserve every experiment's results.


Do not change the primary validation protocol.


---


# 6. Generate Exactly Five Recommendations


For each user:


1. Compute Personalized PageRank scores.
2. Restrict scores to the validated candidate program pool.
3. Rank programs by score.
4. Apply deterministic tie-breaking.
5. Allow previously watched programs according to the shared policy.
6. Fill missing positions using the common training-only popularity fallback.
7. Return exactly five unique, positive program IDs.


Preserve user IDs exactly.


If a validation candidate is absent from the training graph, it may be recommended through the documented fallback or another explicitly evaluated, training-only scoring strategy.


Do not use validation viewing data to resolve unknown candidates.


---


# 7. Evaluate MAP@5


Use the existing Step 3 MAP@5 evaluator.


Report for every configuration:


- Primary MAP@5 across all 1,260 validation users.
- Diagnostic MAP@5 for users with relevant labels.
- Hit Rate@5.
- Top-1 hit rate.

The leaderboard is frozen, so position on it carries no information; only the returned score does. The metric is MAP@{K} with **higher is better**, so 0.00000 is the worst possible score rather than a neutral one — the template's own 0.00000 makes that concrete.

| Next 20% | 40 |

### B. Homework-style evaluation — 50 points

The existing homework criteria apply, scaled to 50 points, covering implementation, report, verification, business analysis and the required records. This quiz does not invent a new subscore breakdown. A high private score does not replace the requirement to implement and compare two methods, justify the strategy, and provide evidence.

75: @lru_cache(maxsize=1024)
76: def stable_day_offset(day):
77:     """Fast path only for Kyiv dates with the same offset throughout the day.
78: 
79:     Transition days use explicit fold/round-trip validation below. The fixed zone
80:     has no same-day pair of offset transitions; no fixed offset is used globally.
81:     """
82:     base = datetime.combine(day, datetime.min.time())
83:     offsets = {(base + timedelta(hours=h)).replace(tzinfo=ZONE).utcoffset()
84:                for h in (0, 12, 24)}
85:     return int(next(iter(offsets)).total_seconds()) if len(offsets) == 1 else None
86:

88: def parse_timestamp(value, schedule=False, fold=None):
89:     pattern = SCHEDULE_PATTERN if schedule else VIEW_PATTERN
90:     if not pattern.fullmatch(value):
91:         raise ValueError(f"Unexpected timestamp format: {value!r}")
92:     if not (0 <= int(value[11:13]) < 24 and 0 <= int(value[14:16]) < 60
93:             and 0 <= int(value[17:19]) < 60):
94:         raise ValueError(f"Out-of-range clock fields: {value!r}")
95:     if fold not in (None, 0, 1):
96:         raise ValueError("Invalid fold")
97:     text = value[6:10] + "-" + value[3:5] + "-" + value[:2] + value[10:] if schedule else value
98:     naive = datetime.fromisoformat(text)
99:     offset = stable_day_offset(naive.date())
100:     if offset is not None:
101:         return int((naive - EPOCH).total_seconds()) - offset
102:     options = {}
103:     for candidate_fold in (0, 1):
104:         aware = naive.replace(tzinfo=ZONE, fold=candidate_fold)
105:         utc = aware.astimezone(timezone.utc)
106:         if utc.astimezone(ZONE).replace(tzinfo=None) == naive:
107:             options[candidate_fold] = int(utc.timestamp())
108:     if not options:
109:         raise ValueError(f"Nonexistent local time in inferred Europe/Kyiv zone: {value}")
110:     if len(set(options.values())) > 1 and fold is None:
111:         raise ValueError(f"Ambiguous local time needs an explicit fold: {value}")
112:     if fold is not None and fold not in options:
113:         raise ValueError("Invalid fold")
114:     return options[fold] if fold is not None else next(iter(options.values()))

133: def parse_view(row):
134:     user, channel, start, end, duration = row

146:     if item < 0 or duration < 0:

152: def union_intervals(spans, window=None):
153:     clipped = []
154:     for start, end in spans:
155:         if end <= start:
156:             raise ValueError("Nonpositive viewing interval")
157:         if window is not None:
158:             start, end = max(start, window[0]), min(end, window[1])
159:         if start < end:
160:             clipped.append((start, end))
161:     merged = []
162:     for start, end in sorted(clipped):
163:         if merged and start <= merged[-1][1]:
164:             merged[-1] = (merged[-1][0], max(end, merged[-1][1]))
165:         else:
166:             merged.append((start, end))
167:     return merged

170: class AiringIndex:
171:     """Sorted positive-ID airings for exactly one channel; fail on ambiguity."""
172: 
173:     def __init__(self, airings):
174:         self.airings = sorted({a for a in airings if a.item > 0 and a.end > a.start},
175:                               key=lambda a: (a.start, a.end, a.item))
176:         if len({a.channel for a in self.airings}) > 1:
177:             raise ValueError("An airing index must contain exactly one channel")
178:         self.starts, self.ends = [], []
179:         last_end = None
180:         for airing in self.airings:
181:             if last_end is not None and airing.start < last_end:
182:                 raise ValueError(f"Conflicting labelled airings: {airing}")
183:             self.starts.append(airing.start)
184:             self.ends.append(airing.end)
185:             last_end = airing.end

188: def match_channel(spans, index, window):
189:     """Optimized interval join; accumulate fragments before applying ANY threshold."""
190:     totals = {}
191:     for start, end in union_intervals(spans, window):
192:         left, right = bisect_right(index.ends, start), bisect_left(index.starts, end)
193:         for i in range(left, right):
194:             airing = index.airings[i]
195:             first, last = max(start, airing.start), min(end, airing.end)
196:             if first < last:
197:                 old = totals.get(airing)
198:                 totals[airing] = Overlap(last - first + (old.seconds if old else 0),
199:                                         min(old.first, first) if old else first,
200:                                         max(old.last, last) if old else last)
201:     for airing, value in totals.items():
202:         if not (0 < value.seconds <= airing.end - airing.start
203:                 and window[0] <= value.first < value.last <= window[1]):
204:             raise AssertionError("Invalid credited seconds or temporal leakage")
205:     return totals

208: def match_views(views, airings, window):
209:     """Small-data API, also used to independently test production matching logic."""
210:     schedules, groups = defaultdict(list), defaultdict(list)
211:     for airing in airings:
212:         schedules[airing.channel].append(airing)
213:     for view in views:
214:         groups[(view.user, view.channel)].append((view.start, view.end))
215:     indexes = {c: AiringIndex(a) for c, a in schedules.items()}
216:     result = {}
217:     empty = AiringIndex([])
218:     for (user, channel), spans in groups.items():
219:         for airing, overlap in match_channel(spans, indexes.get(channel, empty), window).items():
220:             result[(user, *airing)] = overlap
221:     return result

224: def combine_period_matches(first, second):
225:     """Combine disjoint-window overlaps, BEFORE thresholding, for full history."""
226:     result = dict(first)
227:     for airing, value in second.items():
228:         old = result.get(airing)
229:         result[airing] = Overlap(old.seconds + value.seconds,
230:                                 min(old.first, value.first), max(old.last, value.last)) if old else value
231:         if result[airing].seconds > airing.end - airing.start:
232:             raise AssertionError("Period merge double-counted a broadcast")
233:     return result

236: class CoverageIndex:
237:     """Union schedule coverage, including ID zero, for missing-label diagnostics."""
238: 
239:     def __init__(self, spans):
240:         merged = union_intervals(spans)
241:         self.starts = [s for s, _ in merged]
242:         self.ends = [e for _, e in merged]
243:         self.prefix = [0]
244:         for s, e in merged:
245:             self.prefix.append(self.prefix[-1] + e - s)
246: 
247:     def seconds(self, start, end):
248:         left, right = bisect_right(self.ends, start), bisect_left(self.starts, end)
249:         if left >= right:
250:             return 0
251:         return (self.prefix[right] - self.prefix[left]
252:                 - max(0, start - self.starts[left]) - max(0, self.ends[right - 1] - end))

444:     """Aggregate qualifying broadcasts; suitable for one user's rows at a time."""

display.text:
"""Training-only global popularity rankings and exact-five candidate restriction.

No validation labels are accepted by fit_popularity. Each score variant uses the
same deterministic tie-break: distinct training users, training airing count,
then numeric program ID, descending for the first two and ascending for the ID.
"""

from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass
import time

from validation import EvaluationProtocol, training_input

VARIANTS = ("distinct_users", "qualifying_airings", "watched_seconds")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PopularityModel:
    candidates: tuple
    distinct_users: dict
    qualifying_airings: dict
    watched_seconds: dict
    training_sha256: str
    training_window_utc: tuple
    training_rows: int
    training_runtime_seconds: float

    def ranking(self, variant):
        if variant not in VARIANTS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown popularity variant: {variant}")
        scores = {"distinct_users": self.distinct_users,
                  "qualifying_airings": self.qualifying_airings,
                  "watched_seconds": self.watched_seconds}[variant]
        return tuple(sorted(self.candidates,
                            key=lambda item: (-scores.get(item, 0),
                                              -self.distinct_users.get(item, 0),
                                              -self.qualifying_airings.get(item, 0), int(item))))


def fit_popularity(config, candidates=None):
    """Compute three all-user statistics using ONLY registered training rows."""
    started = time.monotonic()
    source = training_input(config)
    candidates = tuple(candidates) if candidates is not None else EvaluationProtocol().candidates
    users_by_program = {}
    airs, seconds = Counter(), Counter()
    rows = 0
    for row in source.rows():
        rows += 1
        users_by_program.setdefault(row.program_id, set()).add(row.user_id)
        airs[row.program_id] += row.qualifying_airings
        seconds[row.program_id] += row.watched_seconds
    distinct = {item: len(user_set) for item, user_set in users_by_program.items()}
    return PopularityModel(tuple(sorted(set(candidates), key=int)), distinct, dict(airs), dict(seconds),
                           source.sha256, tuple(source.window_utc), rows,
                           time.monotonic() - started)


def predictions(model, variant, cohort):
    ranking = model.ranking(variant)
    if len(model.candidates) < 5:
        raise ValueError("Candidate pool must contain at least five programs")
    return {u: ranking[:5] for u in cohort}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    protocol = EvaluationProtocol()
    model = fit_popularity(protocol.config, protocol.candidates)
    print({"training_rows": model.training_rows, "training_seconds": model.training_runtime_seconds,
           "variants": {name: model.ranking(name)[:5] for name in VARIANTS}})

"""Per-user frequency baselines from Weeks 11–20 and common popularity fallback."""

from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
import time

from popularity import PopularityModel
from validation import EvaluationProtocol, training_input

VARIANTS = ("qualifying_airings", "watched_seconds")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PersonalFrequencyModel:
    candidates: tuple
    user_airings: dict
    user_seconds: dict
    training_sha256: str
    training_window_utc: tuple
    training_rows: int
    training_runtime_seconds: float

    def user_ranking(self, user, variant, fallback):
        if variant not in VARIANTS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown personal-frequency variant: {variant}")
        per_user = self.user_airings if variant == "qualifying_airings" else self.user_seconds
        scores = per_user.get(user, {})
        eligible = frozenset(self.candidates)
        personal = sorted((item for item in scores if item in eligible),
                          key=lambda item: (-scores[item], int(item)))
        seen = set(personal)
        # Repeat-allowed: prior programs stay in personal ranking when eligible.
        # Popularity fallback completes remaining slots and also serves cold users.
        personal.extend(item for item in fallback if item in eligible and item not in seen)
        return tuple(personal)


def fit_personal_frequency(config, candidates=None):
    started = time.monotonic()
    source = training_input(config)
    candidates = tuple(candidates) if candidates is not None else EvaluationProtocol().candidates
    airings, seconds = defaultdict(Counter), defaultdict(Counter)
    rows = 0
    for row in source.rows():
        rows += 1
        airings[row.user_id][row.program_id] += row.qualifying_airings
        seconds[row.user_id][row.program_id] += row.watched_seconds
    return PersonalFrequencyModel(tuple(sorted(set(candidates), key=int)),
                                  {u: dict(v) for u, v in airings.items()},
                                  {u: dict(v) for u, v in seconds.items()},
                                  source.sha256, tuple(source.window_utc), rows,
                                  time.monotonic() - started)


def predict(model, variant, cohort, popularity_model, fallback_variant="distinct_users"):
    if model.candidates != popularity_model.candidates:
        raise ValueError("Personal and popularity candidate pools differ")
    if model.training_sha256 != popularity_model.training_sha256 or model.training_window_utc != popularity_model.training_window_utc:
        raise ValueError("Personal and fallback training provenance differs")
    fallback = popularity_model.ranking(fallback_variant)
    result = {}
    for user in cohort:
        result[user] = model.user_ranking(user, variant, fallback)[:5]
    return result


if __name__ == "__main__":
    protocol = EvaluationProtocol()
    from popularity import fit_popularity
    global_model = fit_popularity(protocol.config, protocol.candidates)
    model = fit_personal_frequency(protocol.config, protocol.candidates)
    print({"training_rows": model.training_rows, "training_seconds": model.training_runtime_seconds,
           "variants": {name: model.user_ranking(protocol.cohort[0], name, global_model.ranking("distinct_users"))[:5]
                        for name in VARIANTS}})

11: ## Scope and protocol

13: ### Exact schemas and identity preservation

23: ### Time interpretation and boundaries
24: 
25: **Europe/Kyiv is an evidence-supported inference, not an officially declared competition timezone.** Viewing timestamps are explicitly parsed as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`; schedule starts as `DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM:SS`. Dates and clock fields are validated. Transition-day local times are round-tripped through UTC: nonexistent times are rejected, and ambiguous autumn times require an explicit fold. The supplied periods precede the autumn transition, but that behavior is tested.
26: 
27: Elapsed-time arithmetic uses UTC integer seconds. Broadcast end is **UTC-localized start + elapsed schedule duration**, so adding an hour across the spring clock jump is correct. Viewing endpoints are localized separately, and their elapsed difference must equal the supplied `duraton`. This check succeeded for every source viewing record, including the 117 DST-crossing records identified in Step 1. A cached day offset accelerates ordinary dates; transition dates take the explicit fold/round-trip path.

29: | Partition | Local half-open interval | UTC Unix-second interval |

Test schedule rows contribute availability IDs only and are never joined to user behavior. Full-history outputs are prepared data for possible later fitting; **they must not be used to train a model being evaluated on the Week 21–30 hold-out**.
37: 
38: ### Join, union, and configurable threshold
39: 
40: 1. Stream and validate original files; check their hashes against Step 1 before processing and again afterward.
41: 2. Use a disk-backed sort by `(channel,user,start,end,original_record)`. Remove exact duplicate viewing records by their complete original parsed CSV field values. Preserve original files.
42: 3. Within each user/channel and partition, union overlapping or touching viewing intervals. A continuous session may match several broadcasts; distinct channels are not merged into one artificial viewing sequence.
43: 4. Deduplicate broadcast identities `(channel,start_utc,end_utc,program_id)` in the channel index. Invalid zero-duration broadcasts are excluded. Conflicting overlapping positive-ID airings on a viewed historical channel cause a clear failure rather than silent double credit; none occurred in this run.
44: 5. Match only the same channel and positive half-open interval overlap:
45: 
46:    `max(0, min(view_end,broadcast_end) - max(view_start,broadcast_start))`.

50: 8. Derive user–program pairs by keeping broadcasts whose summed overlap is at least the requested threshold, then aggregating qualifying-broadcast counts, credited seconds, and first/last qualifying watch times for each user and program.

A second **300-second** dataset was actually derived from the same saved overlap cache. No raw interval join was rebuilt for that alternative.
